gloss: landing a catch; unloading; sales revenue

definitions.gloss: landing a catch; unloading fish from a boat
definitions.explanation: The act of bringing caught fish or seafood from a fishing boat to the harbor. Also refers to the quantity or value of fish landed.
The total amount of money earned from sales, especially in retail or market contexts.

examples.japanese: {今朝|けさ}の{水揚|みずあ}げは{豊富|ほうふ}だった。
{港|みなと}でマグロが{水揚|みずあ}げされた。
examples.english: Tuna was landed at the harbor.

examples.japanese: この{漁港|ぎょこう}はサンマの{水揚|みずあ}げ{量|りょう}が{日本一|にほんいち}だ。
examples.english: This fishing port has the highest saury landings in Japan.

examples.japanese: {先月|せんげつ}の{水揚|みずあ}げは{好調|こうちょう}だった。
{年間|ねんかん}{水揚|みずあ}げ{高|だか}が{過去|かこ}{最高|さいこう}を{記録|きろく}した。
examples.english: The annual gross sales set a new record.

examples.japanese: セールのおかげで、{今月|こんげつ}の{水揚|みずあ}げが{伸|の}びた。
examples.english: Thanks to the sale, this month's revenue increased.

notes: Sense 1 is the primary meaning in modern usage and is very common in news about the fishing industry. Common collocations: {水揚|みずあ}げ{量|りょう} (amount landed), {水揚|みずあ}げ{高|だか} (value of catch/sales), {水揚|みずあ}げする (to land/unload). For sense 2, {売|う}り{上|あ}げ (sales) is more commonly used in general business contexts.
